📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In bear life, as in human life, sometimes you just have to take a leap of faith. A brown bear (Ursus arctos) cub hanging around Anan Creek in Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska learned that this summer. Its mom, Gemini, was crossing the creek, and one cub jumped right in. But this cub? Not so sure. It stood waiting at the water’s edge, before jumping in.

It has been revealed that for this forceful leap into the water, the park rangers have awarded Gemini’s little cub with the 2026 Yeet of Faith Award. For those keeping score at home, Gemini won this year’s helicopter mom award.

“Cubs learn at their own pace, and thanks to amazing recreation sites like Anan, we get to witness their tiny triumphs up close,” the rangers write.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of Southeast Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots for wildlife is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears (Ursus americanus) and eight brown bears like Gemini and her cubs. Similar to their chubby counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to gorge on salmon ahead of the long winter, and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear around Anan Creek has their own habits and quirks.

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behaviors.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (501 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Nearly 3 million pages of military records from the War of 1812 are finally online

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (501 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812.
  • Recent findings suggest that while archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the new documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census.
  • “In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley stated in a recent announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812. The project is more than just preservation for preservation’s sake. The roughly 2.8 million pages contain long-forgotten and missing details about 19th century Americans, their families, and their everyday lives.

Recent findings suggest that while archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the new documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census. Patricia Oxley, president of the Federation of Genealogical Societies (FGS), explained the project was also incredibly time-sensitive.

“In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley stated in a recent announcement.

Industry observers note that the somewhat new United States of America declared war on the United Kingdom on June 18, 1812, citing objections to trade restrictions with France amid the Napoleonic Wars, as well as the Royal Navy’s impressment of American sailors. Although the conflict famously included a British attack on Washington D.C. that resulted in the burning of the White House and U.S. Capitol, little shifted geopolitically between the two nations following the ratification of the Treaty of Ghent on February 17, 1815. The U.S. tallied around 15,000 casualties, while the U.K. and Canada saw about 10,700 deaths. Another 9,000 Indigenous fighters died while enlisted between the two sides.

Today’s military records are meticulously documented and stored digitally, but applying for benefits such as pensions was a much more labor-intensive process during the 19th century. With the burden of proof on each applicant, veterans were required to supply lengthy accounts of their service. Each War of 1812 pension file is liable to contain not just combat information, but the names and personal details of fellow soldiers, family members, spouses, and countless other relations.

“Our owners have been asking for the War of 1812 pension records for some time, and I expect this collection to be very popular based on the rich war time detail it contains,” added Brian Hansen, general manager at Fold3, Ancestry’s military records service and National Archives collaborator.

The collection also includes a full-text search feature using handwriting recognition technology. This lets owners explore the files based on every named individual, and not simply the primary veteran applicants. The pension records are currently available for free on Fold3’s website, and are being added to the National Archives catalog on a rolling basis.

Correction 11/20/26 9:30 a.m. EST: A previous version of this article incorrectly stated the pension archive contained around 7 million files. This was based on an initial assessment from researchers in 2010. The article has been updated to reflect the more accurate tally.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Four years after the fall of cryptocurrency partners-in-crime Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, their Icarian story is coming to the small screen twice over.
  • No matter which retelling you tune into, much of the action is sure to take place at Bankman-Fried’s $35 million “crypto frat house” (as CNBC once called it) in The Bahamas, which served as the headquarters of his cryptocurrency exchange FTX at the time of his and Ellison’s arrests for wire fraud and several conspiracy charges in 2022.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Four years after the fall of cryptocurrency partners-in-crime Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, their Icarian story is coming to the small screen twice over. A docuseries about the scandal, The Boy Who Stole Millions?, debuts on Prime Video November 30, and Netflix’s drama series The Altruists premiered November 19.

No matter which retelling you tune into, much of the action is sure to take place at Bankman-Fried’s $35 million “crypto frat house” (as CNBC once called it) in The Bahamas, which served as the headquarters of his cryptocurrency exchange FTX at the time of his and Ellison’s arrests for wire fraud and several conspiracy charges in 2022.

The Orchid building at Albany, The Bahamas.

Bankman-Fried and Ellison met while working at trading firm Jane Street in Manhattan in 2016, and began an on-again, off-again romantic relationship. Bankman-Fried’s first crypto business was the quantitative trading firm he cofounded in 2017, Alameda Research. He went on to found crypto exchange FTX. Ellison, who first began working at Alameda in 2018, became its co-CEO and ran the firm as FTX’s hedge fund.

Bankman-Fried and Ellison moved to The Bahamas in 2021, reportedly motivated by looser COVID-19 pandemic protocols, and “a proactive stance taken by The Bahamas and its regulatory bodies on cryptocurrencies,” Bankman-Fried told Blockworks.

The FTX and Alameda crews encamped at a luxury resort community called Albany. (Tiger Woods and Justin Timberlake are both investors.) Through his companies, Bankman-Fried purchased a penthouse in the sleek Orchid building there, named for its custom cutout façade. Designed by Morris Adjmi Architects, the Orchid’s blue latticework (inspired by Upcoming Orleans ironwork), is unmissable, offering an open-air feel to residents while signaling a layer of privacy to outsiders.

A reception area in the Orchid building.

Sources indicate that bankman-Fried shared his 11,500-square-foot unit with Ellison and eight other FTX and Alameda employees. The apartment has a circular living room, a light-up bar, Italian marble floors, cove lighting, and custom closets. Per a real estate listing obtained by Semafor, Bankman-Fried’s unit had German-engineered windows and doors. Outdoor amenities included a firepit, spa, grill and cooking area, and pool.

The couple attempted to evade culpability for misappropriating $8 billion of FTX customer money, a crime uncovered after Bankman-Fried bought his Bahamas property. Both were convicted of wire fraud and several conspiracy charges. Ellison served 14 months of a 24-month sentence. Bankman-Fried is at the moment serving a 25-year prison sentence and maintains that he is innocent.

In a recent development, to bring this story to life for The Altruists, production designer Todd Fjelsted re-created the infamous penthouse. Several interiors were shot in Vancouver, but scenes requiring a beach or docks were shot in the Dominican Republic.

Julia Garner as Caroline Ellison in a scene from The Altruists filmed in the Orchid set.

According to recent reports, fjelsted and his crew also built miniature replicas of real Albany buildings and a marina complete with a 10-foot remote-control yacht, using forced perspective to shoot them as backdrops. He calls this “the anti-AI set.”.

In a recent development, in the dramatization, coworkers trade crypto in a communal office and party on a balcony overlooking the water. An employee in a hot tub bangs a gong for rounds of speed chess played on fancy sets. Inside, gaming is a major pastime, and there’s a baby grand piano on hand, though no one plays it. In real life, it was reported that Bankman-Fried kept a bean bag under the piano for napping.

Alex Lawther as Sam Trabucco and Anthony Boyle as Sam Bankman-Fried in The Altruists.

Looking to humanize the leads, Fjelsted observed how “insecurities [and] their feelings of a little bit of an imposter syndrome” informed Sam and Caroline’s design choices or lack thereof. Neutrals, sea colors, and palm tree prints made for a better on-camera look, but in real FBI interior photos, Fjelsted saw bedroom walls with powder blue sponge-painted over navy.

Garner and Boyle as Ellison and Bankman-Fried in The Altruists.

Throughout the show’s eight episodes, the penthouse goes from bustling with the excitement of trading to vibrating with panic as the scandal comes crashing down. Eventually, the space is left nearly empty, with just Bankman-Fried and his parents remaining. In 2024, it was reported that Bankman-Fried’s real estate holdings would be sold off in order to pay back his debts, and today, the unit is indeed up for sale.

  • The annual awards recognize hospitals delivering outstanding patient outcomes in specialty care across the United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hospital ratings have become an crucial resource for choosing where to receive care. They influence which doctors patients choose, how far they are willing to travel, and whether they seek care at a different facility.

On October 27, Healthgrades announced the recipients of the 2027 Specialty Excellence Outpatient Awards and Specialty State Rankings.

The annual awards recognize hospitals delivering outstanding patient outcomes in specialty care across the United States. Healthgrades is the leading platform used by Americans for finding a doctor or hospital.

Upcoming research from Healthgrades highlights that hospital quality is increasingly a factor in healthcare decisions.

Sources indicate that around 80% of patients report that when looking for a doctor, the quality of the hospital where they practice matters. Additionally, 7 in 10 patients (68%) say they’re more likely to seek care for a procedure or health condition from a doctor who works at a hospital with high quality ratings.

What’s more, around 71% of patients say they would switch doctors to gain access to a higher-rated hospital.

“Our specialty awards identify the nation’s top-performing hospitals across numerous medical specialties, helping consumers find high quality care tailored to their specific needs,” said Alana Biggers, MD, MPH, medical advisor at Healthgrades.

Healthgrades is owned by RVO Health. By clicking on this link, we may receive a commission. Learn more.

“Navigating the complex healthcare system can feel daunting, but taking a proactive stance to understand where to access superior care can enhance your healthcare journey and overall experience. The ability to make informed decisions about your health — and where to get care — is a cornerstone of self-advocacy, and we are proud to help make that information accessible to all patients.”.

Healthgrades identifies hospitals that deliver exceptional outcomes across common outpatient procedures and specialty conditions.

Finding high quality care is vital, particularly amid a growing gap between top-performing and one-star hospitals.

According to Healthgrades, from 2023 to 2025, if all hospitals had performed at the five-star level from 2023 to 2025:.

“One of the biggest challenges is balancing increasing patient needs with the resources available to healthcare professionals,” Biggers said.

Industry observers note that “Hospitals face workforce shortages, growing administrative responsibilities, financial pressures, and increasing complexity in patient care. Physicians and other healthcare professionals need adequate time and support not only to evaluate and treat patients, but also to communicate results, coordinate follow-up care, and address concerns that arise between visits,” she continued.

“When healthcare teams are adequately supported, they are better positioned to communicate effectively with patients, coordinate care, and address patients’ needs.”.

Biggers said that ensuring equal access to quality healthcare is challenging because of factors such as:.

Industry observers note that hospital closures and reduced services make access even more difficult. Biggers identified a few possible solutions, such as expanding outpatient care, building community partnerships, using telehealth when appropriate, and improving coordination among healthcare providers.

Sources indicate that “Ultimately, providing high quality care requires more than clinical expertise. It requires healthcare systems to invest in their workforce, strengthen care coordination, and create environments where healthcare professionals have the resources they need to provide safe, effective, and patient-centered care,” Biggers said.

“Equally vital, healthcare systems must ensure that patients have meaningful access to these services, regardless of where they live or their socioeconomic circumstances.”.

Healthgrades acknowledges hospitals that excel in three aspects of specialty care:.

Biggers remarked that outstanding hospitals recognize that high quality care extends beyond just treating an illness.

“It involves listening to patients, understanding their individual circumstances, and ensuring they feel respected, informed, and involved in their healthcare decisions,” she noted.

Patients want to find a hospital that excels in the procedures or health conditions relevant to them.

The recipients of the Specialty Excellence Awards are among the top 15% of hospitals specializing in these areas.

Healthgrades evaluated patient outcomes at roughly 4,500 hospitals across 31 common procedures and conditions to reach their decisions.

Among the list of Specialty Excellence Award recipients, Healthgrades also recognizes America’s 100 Best Hospitals for Specialty Care for 11 specialty areas andAmerica’s 50 Best Hospitals for Specialty Care for four specialty areas.

“An outstanding hospital prioritizes both patient care and the people delivering that care,” Biggers told Healthline.

In a recent development, “While clinical outcomes, patient safety, and access to evidence-based treatments are essential measures of quality, I believe hospitals must also invest in workforce development and support. This means ensuring physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals have appropriate staffing levels, adequate clinical and administrative support, and opportunities for continued professional development,” she continued.

In a recent development, healthgrades awards U.S. hospitals that excel at Outpatient Orthopedic Surgery, Outpatient Joint Replacement, andOutpatient Prostate Care.

Outpatient care is one of the fastest-growing areas of healthcare. The number of orthopedic procedures performed in an outpatient environment has grown exponentially in recent years.

From 2020 to 2025, outpatient hip replacement procedures grew by 81%, while inpatient procedures dropped by 75%. Outpatient knee replacements increased by 71% while inpatient volumes decreased by 70%.

“I believe several factors are contributing to the growing demand for outpatient care, including advances in medical technology, a greater emphasis on preventive care, and the increasing need to manage chronic medical conditions,” Biggers stated.

“Many services and procedures that previously required hospitalization can now be safely performed in outpatient settings. Patients also appreciate the convenience of receiving care closer to home and avoiding unnecessary hospital stays,” she added.

To meet the increasing demand for outpatient procedures, Biggers cautioned that healthcare systems must ensure that these services are adequately staffed and supported.

“Effective communication and coordination between outpatient providers, specialists, and hospitals are essential to maintaining continuity and quality of care,” she noted.

State Rankings identify the top three or five hospitals in eligible states across 19 key specialty areas.

It has been revealed that healthgrades is owned by RVO Health. By clicking on this link, we may receive a commission. Learn more.

The rankings are based on clinical performance and build on the 2027 Healthgrades Specialty Excellence Awards Methodology.

State-level specialty care rankings help consumers find outstanding local hospitals for their condition or procedure.

The analysis used Medicare inpatient data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) from 2023 to 2025, and assessed patient outcomes across 31 conditions and procedures.

These outcomes served as the foundation for determining Specialty Excellence Awards and state hospital rankings.

With consumer-facing awards and ratings influencing healthcare decisions, transparency about their methods and limitations remains essential.

Ratings can help patients ask better questions and compare options, but they should complement — not replace — clinical guidance and informed decision making.

The methodologies for each of the specialty awards can be found on the following pages:.

It has been revealed that for more information, Healthgrades’ Specialty Excellence Patient Advocate Center provides access to the information you need to make informed decisions about your care. This resource includes an overview of how Healthgrades picks award recipients, plus a list of the top U.S. hospitals for specialty care.

Sources indicate that to be eligible for a Specialty Excellence Award, hospitals must receive a rating in the required procedures and conditions used to determine the award. Some awards are based on a single procedure, while others are based on a grouping of procedures. To learn more about Healthgrades’ ratings and awards determination process, see the 2027 Specialty Excellence Awards and Ratings Methodology.

Recent findings suggest that turn off reality TV and turn on the bald eagle cams. It’s all the drama you need.

Sources indicate that when internet-famous bald eagle Shadow seemingly welcomed a mysterious upcoming female into his nest earlier this week, many fans have questioned the whereabouts of Kaydee. After the death of Shadow’s longtime partner Jackie in August, he had been spotted spending time with the 4-year-old banded female eagle named KD1 (later renamed Kaydee). It seemed like the eagles might head into mating season as a pair, but after the arrival of a new, large female, it’s unclear how the relationships will all shake out.

Industry observers note that since the appearance of the mystery female, nicknamed Big Beautiful Visitor or BBV by some fans, Kaydee has disappeared from view of Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV)’s two cameras. She was last spotted by the cameras on November 14 in the Roost Tree, according to FOBBV. Despite concerns that she may be injured or had left the area, wildlife photographers have continued to document Kaydee’s presence near Big Bear Lake as recently as November 18.

Photographer Alla Shumko shared photos of Kaydee perched near Massive Bear Lake on November 18. Kaydee’s double bands are visible as she observed a scuffle between younger eagles fighting over fish.

Mating season is well underway, so viewers of FOBBV’s 24/7 livecams have been watching closely for signs that Shadow has selected a new partner. Shadow has worked with both Kaydee and the new eagle on nest maintenance and shared “beaky kisses” with each female, both signs of bonding in bald eagles. Bald eagle mating involves a bit of aerial acrobatics—copulating pairs can be seen in what’s called a “cartwheel display,” in which they lock talons in mid-air while tumbling down to the ground. Male eagles do not have an external phallus, so mating occurs via a touch of cloacas. Vocalizations can typically be heard during the act, which lasts about 7 to 12 seconds, according to Raptor Resource.

According to recent reports, as this is nature, we humans can’t predict or influence who Shadow will pick as a newly introduced partner. Or if he picks at all. All we can do is watch and wait and let nature take its course.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You don't need much of an imagination to picture yourself curled up on one of 7th Avenue's sectionals.
  • According to recent reports, this month, 7th Avenue cut the ribbon on a 3,240-square-foot storefront in a historic cast-iron building at 476 Broome Street.
  • “The main showroom celebrates volume and openness, with soaring ceilings, dramatic columns, and refined architectural detailing,” notes Stinson.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You don't need much of an imagination to picture yourself curled up on one of 7th Avenue's sectionals. One look at the extra deep seats and plush cushions is enough to have you planning your movie marathon—pass the popcorn, please. But even so, a couch is the sort of thing you want to try before you buy. With the opening of a fresh flagship showroom in New York City's SoHo neighborhood, the brand is hoping you'll make a day of it; get comfortable, stay a while.

According to recent reports, this month, 7th Avenue cut the ribbon on a 3,240-square-foot storefront in a historic cast-iron building at 476 Broome Street. It's the 30th brick-and-mortar space in the US and first permanent location in NYC to open since the brand's founding as a direct-to-consumer business in 2022. Co-founder and CEO Billy Shaw says that he and co-founder Josh Stinson decided to put down roots in the Major Apple after seeing the way Latest Yorkers took to their hero product—the "World's Greatest Modular Sofa," they call it—during the years they operated a pop-up shop in the city.

“The main showroom celebrates volume and openness, with soaring ceilings, dramatic columns, and refined architectural detailing,” notes Stinson.

Co-founders Stinson and Shaw sourced design details for the showroom from around the world. “[These items] have an Old-World patina that balances the modern, contemporary aesthetics of our sofas,” indicates Shaw.

According to recent reports, "We were inspired to create 7th Avenue to solve for a frustration we kept hearing from customers: Finding a sofa that was both beautifully designed and genuinely practical for everyday living was surprisingly difficult," Shaw states. (The brand famously uses water-repellent and stain-resistant performance fabrics, and all sofa covers can be removed and thrown in the washing machine for cleaning.) New Yorkers appreciated the modular designs, which can fit into petite elevators and through the narrow doors and hallways ubiquitous in city homes (gotta love a pre-war building!). “Our sofas arrive in individual boxes, making those tight spaces easier to navigate,” he adds.

In a recent development, A store in New York was a no-brainer, but that doesn't mean finding a location was easy. Shaw and Stinson, who is COO, considered addresses in the Flatiron District, where shoppers can bop in and out of home retailers—like Herman Miller, Design Within Reach, ABC Carpet & Home, Crate & Barrel, the list goes on—without leaving a three-block radius. But ultimately they couldn't let go of SoHo's "unmatched" energy. "We wanted to find a place that is grand and historic, paying homage to NYC’s architectural heritage," says Stinson. With 14-foot ceilings and a skylight, "the space on Broome Street creates a sense of openness and grandeur from the moment customers walk through the door.".

Sources indicate that just how durable are 7th Avenue's furniture pieces? During the SoHo store's opening party, guests were encouraged to drop their drinks on the sofas in a “spill lab.”.

In a recent development, shaw and Stinson, who designed the space themselves, say they used the building's architecture to create different vignettes and experiences for guests. The main showroom, for instance, with its dramatic columns and open space, is perfect for showing off 7th Avenue's larger sectionals. Elsewhere, a daybed is nestled into an alcove for a more intimate scene. "We wanted to demonstrate that great furniture design isn't simply about size," states Stinson. "It's about proportion and the relationship between a piece and the space surrounding it.".

The two also wanted to show that "beautiful design should work for real life." "That meant balancing the stateliness of the cast-iron architecture and high ceilings with warm materials, organic textures, and comfortable places to sit," says Shaw.

A light and bright backdrop of European oak and Turkish travertine is dotted with treasures gathered from around the world: coral stone coffee tables quarried from volcanic islands in Indonesia, century-old olive oil jars from Turkey and Morocco, sculptural plants like a Hawaiian dragon tree. "A Queensland Bottle Tree Bonsai, native to Australia and sourced from Los Angeles plant specialists The Plant Daddies, was shaped over two years to achieve its distinctive curved form," indicates Stinson. These details, Shaw adds, have "an Old-World patina that balances the modern, contemporary aesthetics of our sofas.".

Guests readily settled into 7th Avenue's plush sofas at the flagship's opening party.

"We want customers to feel comfortable settling into this beautiful sofa, yet imagining it in their own home and being used in their day-to-day lives," indicates Stinson. At the opening party, props scattered about the furniture brought this idea to life.

For all the finery, 476 Broome Street feels more like someone's home than an art gallery—and that's very on purpose. "We want customers to feel comfortable settling into this beautiful sofa, yet imagining it in their own home and being used in their day-to-day lives," indicates Stinson. The co-founders want visitors to interact with the furniture. Indeed, a cheeky neon sign that reads "Come Spill on Me" hangs over an emerald velvet couch; at the store's opening party, red wine was passed with nonchalance and guests were invited to plop onto a double-wide sofa and pose for photos with an artful disarray of newspapers, a pizza box, and an overturned gag martini glass—no need to take their shoes off.

According to Shaw and Stinson, great design should accommodate the realities of modern life, messy things like kids, pets, and parties. "Our clients appreciate beautiful, thoughtfully designed spaces, but they also want to live in them without hesitation," indicates Shaw. "Ultimately, we feel that luxury should be lived in, not simply admired.".

North Atlantic right whales named after Dolly Parton and Gonzo

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species.
  • It has been revealed that “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, stated in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement.
  • It has been revealed that the 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species. Of those, 20 have officially received spiffy upcoming names from conservationists at the New England Aquarium’s Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life. The researchers curate the annual North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog, and attach personable monikers to a select few baleen cetaceans in order to more easily monitor them. This year, it’s time to wave hello to Dodo, Volcano, and Dolly.

It has been revealed that “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, stated in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement. “It can be hard to relate to Catalog #5299, but a whale named Nibbles is bound to be memorable.”.

It has been revealed that the 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991). The sister whales have a mother named Fenway (Catalog #2791), who was also named in honor of the Boston Red Sox. Grand Slam earned her new name thanks to her three patches of raised tissue known as callosities that resemble the bases on a baseball field. Meanwhile, Slide received their name due to the curved scar on her back that recalls someone sliding through home plate. Other right whale names this year include Goose, Donegal, and even Gonzo for the beloved Muppet.

“Although the names are intended to help researchers at sea, they also give the general public a better understanding of the individual whales,” added Caroline Mowdy, a spokesperson for Whale and Dolphin Conservation (WDC).

Recent findings suggest that collaborators at the WDC also created some lighthearted, yearbook-esque biographies for each whale. For example, Dolly (Catalog #4191), whose callosity looks strikingly similar to the late, great country singer’s larger-than-life hair, apparently loves the song, “Jolene.” Then again, who doesn’t?

In a recent development, “We see these whales and their families grow each year,” said Mowdy. “Knowing them makes the tragedies even more tragic, but it also makes our determination to protect them even stronger.”.

In a recent development, on Monday, the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium revealed that there are roughly 382 North Atlantic right whales, representing a 1.8 percent drop in population size from the 2024 estimate. Their primary threats remain getting tangled in fishing line and vessel strikes.

According to recent reports, however, even amid their struggles, the 2025–2026 right whale calving season saw the most calves born since 2009. A total of 24 calves were born, including a surprising late addition that was spotted in Canada in September.

6 to 8 Cups of Tea Daily May Reduce Heart Disease Risk by 11%

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (622 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that people who regularly drink tea may have an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease, which includes conditions such as stroke, heart disease, and peripheral artery disease.
  • Sources indicate that both black tea and green tea may offer heart health benefits.
  • The lowest overall vascular risk was seen among tea drinkers who were also physically active and didn’t smoke.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that people who regularly drink tea may have an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease, which includes conditions such as stroke, heart disease, and peripheral artery disease. This is according to a study published on October 21 in the Journal of Internal Medicine.

Sources indicate that both black tea and green tea may offer heart health benefits. However, the study reveals an association rather than proving that drinking tea prevents cardiovascular disease.

The lowest overall vascular risk was seen among tea drinkers who were also physically active and didn’t smoke.

The study followed 485,934 people ages 30–79 from the China Kadoorie Biobank for an average of 9 years.

The researchers found that regular tea drinkers had an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease compared with those who did not regularly drink tea. They also observed a 37% lower risk of ischemic stroke and a 17% lower risk of heart attack.

There was no clear link for hemorrhagic stroke or pulmonary heart disease.

Among people who drank tea at least weekly, the lowest estimated risk was seen in those consuming approximately 6–8 cups per day. However, the findings do not establish this as a recommended daily intake.

Amit Blumfield, MD, a cardiologist with Manhattan Cardiology in NYC who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that it is important to remember this is observational data.

Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of drinking black and green tea on lipids and blood pressure showed only modest, non-significant benefits.

The study also had limitations, including self-reported tea consumption and the possibility that other dietary and lifestyle factors influenced the results.

“Overall, tea seems to, maybe, have some cardiovascular benefits without a significant risk, so I favor tea consumption,” he said.

Michelle Routhenstein, a preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished who was not involved in the research, emphasized that the findings do not establish a cause-and-effect relationship between drinking tea and a lower risk of vascular disease.

“Tea can be a helpful addition to a heart-healthy lifestyle, but it is not a substitute for addressing individual cardiovascular risk factors,” she said.

The researchers also found that drinking “burning hot” tea increased the risk of vascular disease by 16%, consistent with previous research raising concerns about the consumption of very hot beverages.

“I recommend enjoying your tea’s potential benefits by letting it cool to a comfortable sipping temperature before you drink it,” noted Routhenstein.

The study examined black, green, Oolong, and other tea types.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers found that black tea revealed a more consistent association with a lower risk of vascular disease, which is contrary to some earlier research. However, they noted that these results don’t establish black tea as superior to green tea, and they don’t mean you should switch tea types.

“Both black and green tea are great choices for your heart health, and neither is definitively better than the other,” said Routhenstein.

“I recommend choosing whichever you enjoy and consuming it consistently, ideally without much added sugar,” Routhenstein noted.

Blumfield also noted that adding sugar or non-sugar sweeteners may change the potential health effects of drinking tea, so the findings should not automatically be extended to sweetened tea beverages.

Some older research suggests there may be additional health benefits to drinking both black and green tea. These benefits may include:.

Routhenstein stated that tea may also support focus and alertness, improve hydration status, and potentially play a role in metabolic health.

“Enjoying tea can be a simple way to incorporate beneficial plant compounds into your day,” she added.

While drinking tea has been considered a health-promoting habit since ancient times, more research is needed to confirm its various health benefits.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Latest data show a substantial nationwide increase in potentially deadly infections caused by drug-resistant pathogens.
  • The updated Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Threats Report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that drug-resistant bacteria and fungi cause approximately 9.7 million infections in the United States each year.
  • The estimated deaths in the United States from these drug-resistant pathogens have also risen from 35,000 to 50,800.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Latest data show a substantial nationwide increase in potentially deadly infections caused by drug-resistant pathogens.

The updated Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Threats Report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that drug-resistant bacteria and fungi cause approximately 9.7 million infections in the United States each year. This is up from 2.8 million in a similar report from 2019.

The estimated deaths in the United States from these drug-resistant pathogens have also risen from 35,000 to 50,800.

The newly introduced report also noted that infections that commonly occur in people in the hospital account for more than 42,000 deaths and cost the U.S. healthcare system more than $12 billion.

Sources indicate that these findings are based on 2023 data. Officials from the CDC remarked that the increase in drug-resistant infections from 2019 partially reflects a real rise in infections caused by certain resistant bacteria and fungi. However, they also noted that data sources and methodologies have changed, and direct comparisons between the two reports shouldn’t be made.

“These numbers are alarming by any measure but are particularly sobering when infectious diseases physicians connect real patients with these statistics in their everyday experience,” Wendy Armstrong, MD, President of the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), said in a statement.

In a recent development, the CDC report highlighted 19 drug-resistant pathogens responsible for the 9.7 million annual infections. Four of these pathogens are classified as urgent threats, 13 as serious threats, and 2 as concerning.

The CDC also maintains a watch list that currently includes six pathogens.

The four pathogens classified as urgent threats are:.

William Schaffner, MD, a professor of the Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, told Healthline that the reason for this increase in superbugs is, “Overuse of antibiotics; using them for too long or in circumstances where they do not offer a benefit.”.

“An example of the latter is the antibiotic treatment of common viral respiratory infections — antibiotics have no effect on viral infections. The widespread use of antibiotics kills off those bacteria that are susceptible to antibiotics, but then can leave a few bacterial survivors that are resistant to the effect of the antibiotics, resulting in the spread of these resistant strains,” he said.

Monica Gandhi, MD, a professor of medicine at the University of California, San Francisco, agreed and added, “This widespread use leads to selective drug pressure on the pathogen to evolve resistance to these antibiotics, making them harder to treat.”.

“The risk to public health from these bugs is substantial. In fact, the World Health Organization (WHO) estimates up to 5 million deaths from these bugs worldwide every year, making these a substantial public health threat,” stated Gandhi.

Candida auris tops the list of urgent threats.

According to recent reports, cases have increased nearly tenfold since the first detection in hospitals 10 years ago. This includes a more than 50% jump between 2022 and 2023.

Sources indicate that candida auris is a fungus that is almost completely resistant to one class of antifungal medications. It has also shown emerging resistance to the other two classes.

This fungus is often found on people’s skin, spreads rapidly in healthcare settings like hospitals, and affects some of the most vulnerable individuals.

CRE is a family of multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens. They have become increasingly difficult to treat and can share resistance with other bacteria.

These bacteria also pose a significant threat to people in hospitals, especially those with devices such as ventilators and catheters. A recent study found that CRE cases at U.S. hospitals increased by 18% between 2019 and 2023.

While those in hospitals are especially vulnerable to CRE, 67% of the cases in 2023 were in the community. However, some of these cases may have occurred in people with recent exposure to healthcare.

Neisseria gonorrhoeae is the bacterium that causes gonorrhea, which is one of the most common sexually transmitted infections.

The CDC report noted that only a few antibiotics can effectively treat this infection.

Without effective treatment, gonorrhea can lead to:.

There are ways you can help prevent these superbugs:.

“[One] way individuals can help prevent the evolution of these superbugs is to not ask for antibiotics from their providers or urgent care settings in the setting of a viral infection,” said Gandhi.

Experts and organizations like the CDC are working together to find ways to reduce the spread of these superbugs.

“Professional organizations and hospitals are educating their doctors and staff about the antibiotic resistance problem and have created reviews of practice patterns to encourage the appropriate use of antibiotics,” stated Schaffner.

Gandhi added that organizations should institute procedures, such as “antimicrobial stewardship programs,” to ensure that providers do not prescribe antibiotics for non-bacterial infections and narrow antibiotics as soon as possible.

The Pioneering Antimicrobial Subscriptions to End Upsurging Resistance (PASTEUR) Act aims to revitalize antibiotic and antifungal development by changing the way the federal government pays for novel antimicrobials.

This act was reintroduced in Congress in February and is presently under review.

The focus on reducing the spread of superbugs and developing latest antibiotics is vital.

In a recent development, “You really cannot have all the benefits of modern medicine, even outside the realm of infectious diseases, without effective antibiotics. It all goes away,” Haley Ann Pritchard, MD, medical director of infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship at Eskenazi Health Hospital, said in a statement.

Sources indicate that even if you pride yourself on eating whole foods and cooking healthy meals, it can still be super hard to get all of the vitamins and minerals your body needs. Plus, your nutrient needs change as you age.

For instance, “as women navigate through the wonderful world of the menopause transition, there are changes, health-wise, that happen,” indicates Leslie Bonci, RD, a sports dietitian based in Pittsburgh. As your hormone levels start to decrease, you may be more likely to lose bone density and muscle mass. When these changes happen, “there are certain nutrients that are going to be needed more than others,” she adds. That’s when it can be helpful to turn to a supplement.

Meet the experts: Leslie Bonci, RD, is a sports dietitian based in Pittsburgh. Navya Mysore, MD, is a primary care physician, women's health expert, and WH advisory board member based in Fresh York City.

Knowing which supplements you should take in each stage of life may be complicated, but we found the right experts to simplify everything. Consider this your supplement roadmap.

First, have a conversation with your primary care physician—they should know about all of the medications and supplements you’re presently taking or are considering. Your doc will help you ensure supplementation is the best course of action after considering your holistic health care blueprint. Then, they can rule out any potential medication interactions and decide which dosage is best, says Navya Mysore, MD, a primary care physician, women's health expert, and WH advisory board member based in New York City.

Here are some of the most common interactions, per Dr. Mysore and Bonci:.

You also might want to get blood work done before starting a supplement, especially if you think you may have a deficiency. “Checking things like iron stores (ferritin), vitamin D, or B12 can tell you if you actually need a supplement and how much,” states Dr. Mysore. However, you don’t need blood work if you’re just taking a basic prenatal or multivitamin.

According to recent reports, just remember: “Supplements are a complement to—not a replacement for—eating,” Bonci notes. They’re just one piece of the puzzle; in order to live your healthiest, longest, best life, you’ll want to make sure you’re eating nutritiously and exercising consistently.

Sorry to our gummy lovers out there: “Capsules usually win—they tend to absorb better and have fewer fillers,” indicates Dr. Mysore. “Tablets are fine but a bit more variable.” Unfortunately, gummies are often underdosed and may not include key nutrients like iron, she adds. This 500 kWh energy storage system runs on retired EV batteries

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (655 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road.
  • Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.
  • Each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road. Moment Energy’s upcoming Nova battery storage system puts those packs to work on commercial sites. And when a pack wears out, it can be swapped without pulling out the whole system.

Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.

Each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power. It has a 2.94 m by 1.80 m (9.7 x 5.9 ft) footprint, and units can be linked together for projects in the tens of megawatt-hours. A site could charge the batteries when electricity is cheaper or when its solar panels are producing more than it needs, then draw on that power when demand spikes or the grid goes down.

Recent findings suggest that nova can use packs from different EV models, even when those packs have aged at different rates. Moment’s battery management software tracks how each pack is doing. As packs wear out, the company can replace them while leaving the enclosure and concrete pad in place. Moment says its pack replacement service could keep a system in service for more than 20 years.

“We see a future where reengineered EV batteries become essential infrastructure for powering businesses and onshoring manufacturing and supply chains. Nova brings that vision to life, combining safety, engineering, and North American manufacturing to deploy the safest and highest-performance batteries ever made: EV batteries to supercharge our aging grid,” mentioned Edward Chiang, co-founder and CEO of Moment Energy.

Recent findings suggest that moment Energy says Nova is the first storage system built from retired EV batteries to earn both UL 1973 certification for the batteries and UL 9540 certification for the complete system. It was also tested under UL 9540A, which looks at how a battery fire can spread. The factory itself is certified under UL 1974, which covers how used batteries are assessed and graded for reuse.

Sources indicate that that matters for businesses with limited space. Nova is designed to sit outdoors alongside the buildings it serves. It uses liquid cooling, detects smoke, heat, and flammable gases, and is rated to operate from −13F to 122F (−25C to 50C).

Industry observers note that moment Energy also says an independent review found that Nova meets US federal sourcing restrictions tied to the clean electricity investment tax credit. Those rules are one part of determining whether a project qualifies for the credit.

Orders are open, and Moment Energy expects the first units to ship in Q1 2027 for deployments across North America.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even though your holiday tree (probably) only comes out once a year, choosing the right artificial Christmas tree for your home is key to set a truly festive vibe.
  • Our list below includes pre-lit trees that take the guesswork out of nostalgic spruces and even an enticing winter white design.
  • Reviewer: Divya Viswanathan, VP, commerce portfolio lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even though your holiday tree (probably) only comes out once a year, choosing the right artificial Christmas tree for your home is key to set a truly festive vibe. If you’re already committed to the faux lifestyle or are just dipping your toes in, the perfect tree is out there for you and your priorities. Maybe you want something bold and full of personality like the iconic Rockefeller tree in Newly introduced York City. Perhaps you’re looking to go classic with a full lighting system included or something to match your favorite wreaths. No matter your preference, there’s a good chance that once you go faux, you’re never going back to the real deal. After all, there’s no watering involved, cleanup is a breeze, and easy storage is usually part of the design.

Our list below includes pre-lit trees that take the guesswork out of nostalgic spruces and even an enticing winter white design. And to really achieve a professional-looking holiday home, we’ve tapped experts like Kendall Jenner’s holiday floral designer Jeff Leatham and AD-darling designer Shea McGee for exclusive tips on how to level up any faux tree.

Reviewer: Divya Viswanathan, VP, commerce portfolio lead.

This big, beautiful tree is inspired by the Fraser Fir. Known for its rich, dark green coloring and full silhouette, this tree is native to the Appalachian Mountains and has the distinction of being the type of tree most often used as the official White House Christmas tree.

To be honest, we can’t tell the difference between Balsam Hill’s faux version and the real thing. BH's impressive “true needle” foliage features 40 variations of branch types throughout and the effect is incredibly realistic.

Sources indicate that the tree is available just about any height and light variation you could want, all of which feature an easy plug system. Easy plug trees have all the light strands plugged into the center pole, so all you have to do is place the three sections together and plug the tree into an outlet. There’s no need to ever unplug or take off any light strands.

The style pictured above is “color + clear,” which allows you to switch between multicolored lights and white lights via remote. For pre-lit trees with a single lighting style, there is an attached foot pedal to turn the lights on and off. The Twinkly light style features built-in app-controlled smart lights from Twinkly.

Reviewer: DaVonne Bacchus, contributor.

Recent findings suggest that this beauty looks like it was plucked right off the tree farm, but all you have to do is just pull it out of the box. Speaking of, let your tree breathe for a day or two after you take it out of the box. That way, the branches can fluff up on their own before you decorate the tree. The tree features hinged branches, making setup and teardown straightforward (just push each hinge down and pop into a storage bag). If you’re looking for a large tree, and a full tree but don’t want to spend a fortune, this is a good, solid pick from The National Tree Firm. The National Tree Company has been making holiday trees and decorations for more than 60 years, and they have plenty more styles to choose from on Amazon and Wayfair.

Reviewer: Stewart Savin, senior SEO analyst.

It has been revealed that like a real-life Douglas Fir, this faux tree is designed to have a darker hue than other evergreens. Its needles are also longer and flatter than other evergreen varieties, growing out on either side of each branch rather than all the way around it.

Reviewer: Pujah Shah, global director of audience development, analytics & social.

King of Christmas is a holiday-focused brand in the business of memory-making, with a vast inventory of artificial trees, garlands, and decorations to get your home in the Christmas spirit. The brand provides helpful written guides on assembling, shaping, and storing your tree, as well as video tutorials for a more visual learning experience. King of Christmas also donates thousands of trees to underprivileged families and communities impacted by natural disasters each year. The brand’s pre-lit Alpine Fir, a species native to Washington state, feels like spending the holidays in the Pacific Northwest, and allows you to enjoy festive vibes minus the maintenance. While pricing leans on the higher end, each faux tree is handcrafted to mirror the distinct shape, color, and growth pattern of real branches.

Reviewer: Andrea Lewis, contributor.

Recent findings suggest that another one of the prettiest pre-lit Christmas trees is this Blue Spruce. The full foliage on this fake tree includes realistic needles in blue-green and silvery hues paired with light brown stems, just like an authentic Blue Spruce. Like all Balsam Hill trees, it comes with an off-season storage bag, protective gloves to use while shaping the tree branches, and extra bulbs.

Reviewer: Brie Schwartz, commerce director Glamour.

Sources indicate that another tried and true, super affordable option straight from Amazon. We appreciate our contributor Brie Schwartz’s approach to the fake tree game. Instead of spending big bucks going for a super realistic tree, she aims for over-the-top flocking and lots of lights to lean into the fact that she prefers the faux variety (and to have her tree up for as long as humanly possible for the season). Go big or go home, right? If Schwartz’s approach rings true to you, too, this might be the perfect tree for your household.

Reviewer: Kate McGregor, commerce market editor.

We’ve turned to Quince time and time again for their high quality, yet affordable bedding and soft goods over the years. This artificial spruce is the newest addition to our catalog of tested items from the brand. (Fun fact: It’s even the main image of this story in case you were wondering which faux tree made it as our model this year). Quince’s take on a spruce employs an interesting branch design: The back end of each limb features bushier evergreen bunches while the front-portion presents tips that look more realistic. This clever system actually makes the tree look more lush from within while still maintaining the appearance of something life-like on the surface. Commerce market editor Kate McGregor noted in her review that the tree did give off a fuller look, and was especially handsome once decked out with a merrily maximalist slate of ornaments from some of our favorite holiday hubs like John Derian and Anthropologie. Just be mindful that the more realistic branch segments can leave a semi-sticky residue on your hands (an issue you’d have with real tree too, we might add).

Reviewer: Lauren Arzbaecher, commerce producer.

Let us set expectations here: For a tree that’s under $100, you are probably not going to find the highest quality option for your Christmas tree. That said, we wanted to put one to the test to see how it held up in person. If you are looking to prioritize price over super realism, we think this option makes a lot of sense.

Reviewer: Stewart Savin, Senior commerce SEO analyst.

Sources indicate that unconventional tree colors—like gold, silver, or white—are smart options if your taste favors a non-traditional Christmas tree. It brings all the drama but doesn’t pretend to be something it’s not. This all-white Kingswood fir tree won’t dampen any pastel-forward design schemes in the way something with a more authentic evergreen look might. Plus, the snow-like white needles provide a neutral canvas for making your ornaments stand out. Tester Stewart Savin liked that the slim design of her seven foot-tall selection can fit into more narrow crevices, though it’s available in seven-and-a-half, nine, and 12-foot options with wider diameters. A disciple of Kathy Hilton’s design philosophy—that every room deserves a unique tree set up during the holiday season—Savin intends on keeping the Dunhill Fir from the Holiday Isle she tested last year as her main tree, and this smaller silhouette with “winter wonderland vibes” in her bedroom or sunroom.

It’s full enough to feel cozy, and the texture and shape of the branches mirror the real thing nicely. The two places I think it would be more convincing are the needles and overall color. Instead of being tapered, the needles are a bit more fringe-like, with square ends. Personally, I think the color of the tree should be a bit darker with a somewhat brown undertone to make it look more natural than a solid evergreen.

It has been revealed that shopping producer Lauren Arzbaecher’s Treetopia prelit faux balsam was a substantial upgrade from her under-$100 Best Choice pick that’s also named on this list. While Arzbaecher noted in her review that the Best Choice option is “nice enough if you’re looking to get a larger tree on a budget,” it didn’t really achieve a realistic appearance: “Up close, the look of the branches on this tree read less like needles and more like green fringe,” she told us. At $200, Treetopia’s artificial tree is still considered one of the “budget options” on our list, but Arzbaecher noticed quite a difference. “My old tree was incredibly sparse (we’re talking putting Charlie Brown to shame) so this is definitely an upgrade,” she says. “The branch tips go about ¾ of the way in towards the center of each section, which makes it appear fuller. It may have even converted me to a pre-lit devotee.”.

Reviewer: Emma Tubbs, audience development manager.

How easy was it to assemble your tree (on a scale of 1-10, with 10 being the easiest)? 6.

What was the quality of the tree packaging? Will you be able to store your tree for future years? The tree was packaged well in a cardboard box, and I’ll definitely be able to store it in the box at the end of the season.

In a recent development, how long did it take to fluff and prepare your tree? Did you see a lot of needle loss in the process? The most time-consuming part of the assembly process was unfurling and fluffing the tree, but there was very minimal needle loss. I spent about 40 minutes setting it up but roughly 35 minutes of that was fluffing the many sections. The lights that came already incorporated into the tree were twisted around each section very tightly, so I had to spend a good amount of time untangling the lights so that I could fully fluff it up.

Sources indicate that did your tree come with lights or decor? If so, how easy was it to install? (on a scale of 1-10, with 10 being the easiest)? The tree came pre-lit, which is nice, but as I noted, the lights were wrapped so tightly that it took a bit to loosen them so I could fluff the tree. I’m giving it an 8 since it did save some time that it came pre-lit, but it wasn’t totally seamless.

According to recent reports, did your tree live up to your expectations and was the size accurate? Yes, it definitely lived up to my expectations! I specifically wanted a slimmer tree so I wouldn’t have to rearrange my living room too much, and this was the perfect width. The 7.5-foot height is perfect for my tall ceiling, and the tree is slim but still full and realistic-looking so it doesn’t look gangly.

How full is the tree (scale of 1-10, with 10 being the fullest)? 6—since the tree is intentionally more slim and compact, it’s not luxuriously full, but once fluffed up, you can’t see any of the inner metal parts that might make it look artificial otherwise.

It has been revealed that how realistic is the tree? (on a scale of 1-10, with 10 being the most realistic)? 6—up close, you can see that the needles are plastic, but the overall fullness and structure of the tree make it look authentic otherwise. The metal components that make up the frame are hidden in the interior column, which definitely helps. The base is metal and clearly artificial, but I always put a skirt around my tree (even when I’ve had a real one) so that aspect is also naturally concealed.

Puleo International is another well-known name in the artificial tree game, selling at outlets like Amazon, Wayfair, Home Depot, and Lowe's. The brand’s slim Fraser fir was exactly what tester Emma Tubbs was after: “I wanted a slimmer tree so I wouldn’t have to rearrange my living room too much, and this was the perfect width,” she says. The tree’s versatile look and approachable price point also helped it overtake the Best Choice Products Pencil Christmas Tree for our ‘Best Slim Tree’ pick. “The 7.5-foot height is perfect for my tall ceiling, and the tree is slim but still full and realistic-looking so it doesn’t look gangly,” says Tubbs.

We always research products thoroughly before including them, and test every single one. Our reviews are thorough, in-depth, and honest. We put ourselves in the shoes of the shopper (because most of the time, we are the ones shopping!), and make sure that we’re answering the questions that we would want answered in the buying process.

Industry observers note that we favored natural-looking trees that are easy to set up. We also took shipping into account and tested trees that arrive not only in style, but with speed.

All trees that were reviewed were unboxed, set up (and lit up) by our contributors. They lived with trees and experienced all they had to offer firsthand, so that they could share the real deal with our readers.

What Size Christmas Tree Is Right for Me?

First and foremost, the height of your fake Christmas tree should depend on the height of your ceiling. A good rule of thumb is to keep your tree at least one-and-a-half feet lower than your ceiling, otherwise, it will look crowded. “I like to leave about six to12 inches between the top of the tree and the ceiling, so it feels intentional, not squeezed in,” says Shea McGee (more on the designer’s holiday advice below). Both McGee and Jeff Leatham, the floral designer who helped mastermind Kendall Jenner’s festive holiday house, agree that seven to eight feet hits a sweet spot in most homes. “The goal is balance: A tree that feels full and joyful but still lets the room breathe,” says McGee.

Who Should Buy Fake Christmas Trees?

Some people want to avoid the hassle (and extra cost) of buying a fresh tree each year, while others are allergic to real trees or are concerned about the fire safety hazard that comes along with real trees (they can become highly flammable as they dry out). Others (including people with pets) know that a real Christmas tree can be bait for disaster. Fresh or faux is really a matter of personal preference, and anyone who wants a fake Christmas tree should go for it. Leatham points out that in faux trees, the branches don’t drop, the coloring stays vibrant, and there’s often more structure to add extra ornaments.

Is It Better to Get a Pre-Lit Tree Or to Do It Yourself?

Choosing if you want your tree pre-lit is one of the first decisions you’ll make when navigating the vast artificial tree world. Pre-lit options are the preference of holiday decor gurus like Leatham. “Always, always, always go for prelit—it makes the tree look more full and realistic,” he tells us. Our editors like that pre-lit Christmas trees are convenient to set up (opposed to blindly garlanding string lights) and how they help guarantee your lighting scheme will look uniform. That stated, drawbacks include potentially difficult repairs. While you can easily unstring removable lights to troubleshoot, built-in LEDs might pose bigger technical complications. On the other hand, stringing your own lights may be a more complex, time-consuming process, but you’ll ultimately have more control over which areas of your tree are spotlighted.

How Should You Decorate Your Christmas Tree?

It has been revealed that you’ve gotten your tree up, fluffed the branches, and poured yourself a nice cup of hot cocoa or eggnog to celebrate—now comes the fun part: decorating. While there’s no right way to decorate your Christmas tree, we looked through our archives for some tips and tricks to give your setup some extra sparkle.

Recent findings suggest that if your mentality is “more is more,” your holiday hero will be Kathy Hilton, who greeted AD back in 2021 with four artificial Christmas trees decked out with all the bells and whistles (emphasis on the bells). One tip we’d steal from Hilton is the idea that the decorations don’t have to go up all at once. “I normally start decorating in October, then keep adding until December,” states Hilton.

Kendall Jenner, on the other hand, favors a more traditional tree, dipped in nostalgic classics like tinsel, twinkle lights, and vintage Christopher Radko ornaments that were passed down by her mother, Kris. Her designer reveals that she even loves stringing popcorn for the tree and dried orange slices on garlands. “Every year, more and more of my clients want more traditional holiday decorations that they can invest in, collect, and pass on to other generations,” says Leatham. “I love that idea of seeing the same ornaments every year and having them bring back wonderful memories.” Since we have a feeling you have your own collection of heirloom Christmas decorations that have been collecting dust, we’d look to the supermodel for inspiration.

According to recent reports, color scheming your ornament display is one way to set yourself apart from the pack. “Red and green are traditional Christmas colors, but I love to break away from tradition and use bright jewel tones to create a dramatic and sophisticated look for the holiday season,” says Annie Sloan, color expert and creator of Chalk Paint. Stylist Dorcia Kelley of Kelle Miles Studio also suggests using a planter instead of a traditional tree stand or skirt for a modern look. “When hanging ornaments, you want to make sure you’re hanging it towards the end of the branch instead of right at the tip. This way, they’ll be more stable,” she says.

According to recent reports, we also recommend playing with shapes, textures, and finishes to create as much interest as possible. AD’s perfect Christmas tree (pictured at the top of this article) features lots of vintage-inspired John Derian ornaments that bring on the kitsch, accented with classic ball ornaments in a range of sizes to create depth and dimension. A color palette of muted blue and bold metallic hues complement the deep green branches while slivers of silver tinsel add holiday pizzazz.

According to recent reports, fluffing your artificial Christmas tree is the key to convincingly faking the real thing. Most of the time, your tree will arrive with all the branches up-turned straight out of the box, and you’ll first want to mount the tree in its stand or collar. Next comes the actual fluffing—as reviewer Pujah Shah mentioned, it’s a smart idea to wear some work gloves to avoid any pricking that might occur while you’re working through the branches. Starting at the bottom, you’ll fan the largest branches down, layer by layer, until you reach the very top (where the branches become much shorter). If your branches have smaller tips built in, we like the center-right-left method of starting toward the base of the tree and positioning the smaller tips first center, next towards the right, and lastly towards the left, until you’ve reached the end. After that, you’ll go branch by branch, noticing that your tree looks full and much more lush with each adjustment. Afterwards, all that’s left to do is make any minor fixes to eliminate bald spots and voila!

What’s the Best Real Christmas Tree to Buy?

Again, that’s completely a matter of personal preference. Trees come in a variety of hues, some with a dark green, some with a blue tint, and others with a bright shade. Some have spiky needles while others are soft to the touch. Trees vary by geographical region and what's native to your area, but some of the most popular options used as Christmas trees across the U.S. include the Fraser Fir, Balsam Fir, Douglas Fir, and Blue Spruce (all of which are available in faux varieties, as well!).

How Does the Lifetime Cost of a Faux Tree Compare to Annually Buying a Real Tree?

While how much your real Christmas tree costs will vary depending on its size as well as where you live in the United States, expect to spend anywhere from $40 to well over $100. In a few years, that running total will start to cost you, but with an artificial tree, you’ll pay the total cost up front. High-quality trees can also last you up to 15 years, making the sometimes extravagant price tags more digestible, especially in the later years when you’re no longer burdened with figuring out the logistics of strapping that netted Douglas Fir onto the car roof.

What Is Flocking and How Do You Do It?

Sources indicate that flocking refers to the process of dusting your artificial Christmas tree with a powdery white overcoat to mimic the appearance of fresh snowfall. Some trees—like the Yaheetech tree Brie Schwartz tested—come pre-flocked, but if you prefer a DIY moment, ready-to-flock sprays are also available at most significant box retailers. We like Balsam Hill’s guide to flocking your tree, which details a recipe for homemade flocking, as well as all the safety precautions you’ll want to take: Like wearing protective gear, flocking in a well-ventilated environment, and ensuring you’re using non-hazardous materials. (Though if your budget allows, we think it might be best to invest in one of the brand’s ready-flocked trees.).

King of Christmas vs. Balsam Hill.

In a recent development, in the grand scheme of artificial Christmas trees, King of Christmas and Balsam Hill are widely known as the crème de la crème, thanks to their realistic appearance, convenient setup, and thoughtful extras like complimentary storage bags for the off-season. While both fall into the category of more luxuriously-priced holiday decor, Balsam Hill’s price points are slightly higher ($349 to $4,000+ while King of Christmas ranges from $229 to $3,000+).

In our own quests for the most elite faux trees, we’ve also tried both brands. Commerce vice president Divya Viswanathan called Balsam Hill’s Fraser Fir “the Christmas tree of my dreams,” while contributor Andrea Lewis previously called her Blue Spruce from the brand “a lovely addition to our holiday traditions—elegant, easy to manage, and captures that cozy, Christmas air perfectly.” AD’s global director of audience development Pujah Shah became a King of Christmas convert last holiday after testing the brand’s Alpine Fir tree. “I wanted something tall, sleek, and a little bit dramatic that felt intentional in a modern space but still cozy enough for family chaos—it nails both,” says Shah. We think that both brands are great options—it’s hard to beat how realistic Balsam Hills designs are, and holiday floral designer and one of our experts, Jeff Leatham even named King of Christmas as his favorite brand. To choose the right brand for you, we recommend figuring out what will suit your space and your decorations, as well as establishing a price point you’re comfortable with.

In a recent development, we tapped the designer and creative force behind one of our favorite interior brands, McGee & Co., on the best ways to make your artificial Christmas tree really pop this season. Read on for her advice on how to make merry with a beautiful, yet intentional holiday set up.

Is There Such a Thing as an Ideal Sized Christmas Tree?

“When you’re choosing a tree, the ideal size really depends on your space. I like to leave about 6–12 inches between the top of the tree and the ceiling, so it feels intentional, not squeezed in. For most standard spaces, a 7-7.5-foot tree hits the sweet spot. If you have tall ceilings, you can absolutely go bigger—9-12 feet fills the volume beautifully. And in smaller rooms, a slimmer silhouette keeps things festive without overwhelming the layout. The goal is balance: A tree that feels full and joyful but still lets the room breathe.”.

What are Some of the Design Benefits of Choosing an Artificial Christmas Tree Versus a Real One?

In a recent development, “I love the flexibility an artificial tree gives you. You know exactly what shape and fullness you’re getting, and the branches stay right where you want them—which makes decorating so much easier and more polished. They also hold up all season long, which is great if you like to decorate early. And of course, you can reuse them year after year, which means you can invest in the style you love and bring it back every holiday.”.

How Do You Make an Artificial Christmas Tree Look More Realistic?

According to recent reports, “Start with a tree that already has a natural, realistic base—good branch texture goes a long way. From there, keep your palette cohesive so the whole tree feels curated instead of busy. I love layering garlands because they add that organic movement you see in real trees. Then finish with meaningful ornaments, ribbon, and a few organic touches—like dried citrus or pinecones. Those add warmth and authenticity, making even a faux tree feel beautifully lifelike.”.

“Both options have their place. A pre-lit tree is all about ease—the lights are perfectly placed, and you get that warm glow the minute you plug it in. It’s great if you want a beautiful tree without the extra steps. An unlit tree gives you more creative freedom. You can layer different styles of lights, change the mood from year to year, and really customize the look. It takes a bit more time, but it can feel incredibly intentional. So, if you want quick and polished, go pre-lit. If you love the process of styling every detail, unlit is the way to go.”.

Sources indicate that the easiest way to make your artificial Christmas tree look like a real tree is to, well, cover it up. Go heavier on the decorations this year: Think garland, Christmas lights, pinecones, ornaments, a tree topper, etc. We're talking the works. Check out our go-to holiday decor tips that will make the best Christmas trees look even more magical.

It’s affordable in bulk, doubles as a garland, and covers quite a bit of real estate from low to high. And who doesn’t love a bow? We pulled an option to satisfy the minimalists as well as some embellished trim that’s got major maximalist appeal.

A dead giveaway—no pun intended—that your tree’s a fake is the base: that plastic, mechanical-esque tree stand. Cover that metal stand up with a festive tree skirt (or basket!) as you would with real Christmas trees.

Industry observers note that if your tree doesn’t have pre-strung lights, head to the holiday aisle for some white or multicolored lights. Some of our favorites include unconventional and more delicate-looking lights that don’t necessarily scream “Christmas.” They’ll draw the eye to the center of the tree and take the attention off of the branches. Besides, you can never have too many lights in your home decor during the holiday season.

When scouting out ornaments for your tree, look for options with serious heirloom potential. Kendall Jenner’s Christopher Radko’s classic ornament collection is a good example—and Etsy sellers have troves of vintage ornaments to start your own traditions or recreate the supermodel’s holiday style. These miniature bulbs we found at Terrain are a fun way to create more depth when paired with larger balls, and we like that the different colors really pop when your tree is lit. We also turned to John Derian for gorgeous, traditional options pictured on our tree.
